items.title: Continuous paths give vanishing transport cost

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib path-law transport supplement: Continuous paths give vanishing transport cost
source.attribution: Original shared library statement; chapter placement provides reading context, without numbered textbook-theorem credit.

items.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). For every fixed \(s\in T\), the Kantorovich cost with cost \(c\) from \(\mu_t\) to \(\mu_s\) tends to zero as \(t\to s\). The limit is in the extended nonnegative reals.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.

obligations.label: Continuous paths give vanishing transport cost

bindings.boundary: The cost need not be a metric or symmetric. Compactness and the finite continuous cost are retained. This is a limit at each fixed time, without a quantitative rate.

items.title: A transport estimate gives joint continuity

source.anchor: Original Samplinglib path-law transport supplement: A transport estimate gives joint continuity
source.attribution: Original shared library statement; chapter placement provides reading context, without numbered textbook-theorem credit.

items.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). Let \(F\) be a normed additive commutative group, \(U:T\times E\to F\) any field, and \(L\in\mathbb R\). Suppose the bound below holds for every pair \((t,x),(s,y)\). Then \(U\) is jointly continuous. Here \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) denotes the probability couplings. The map \(\operatorname{toReal}\) takes the ordinary real value at finite inputs and sends \(\infty\) to zero; the costs \(Q(t,s)\) here are finite by compactness and the explicit same-sample coupling.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.
\(F\) is a normed additive commutative group; no scalar action or completeness is required.
The displayed estimate holds for all pairs in \(T\times E\), with one real constant \(L\). No sign assumption on \(L\), or prior regularity of \(U\), is required.

obligations.label: A transport estimate gives joint continuity

bindings.boundary: The estimate is an explicit input to this general continuity principle. A model application must establish it separately. The proof uses continuity of the extended-real toReal map at zero; no separate finite-cost premise is inserted.
